name: Our Blood Institute (OBI) (Partner)
assessment: Interviews at OBI are generally described as easy with basic behavioral questions like describing a time you went outside procedure to make something happen. The overall hiring process typically takes about one week and is rated favorably by candidates
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
Education Minimum: High school diploma or GED required.
Required Experience:
No specific years required, though 1 year of customer service, telemarketing, or sales is preferred
Pleasant voice and professional phone manner
Preferred Experience:
Customer service, telemarketing, or sales background
Outbound calling experience
Required Skills:
Clear verbal communication and good listening skills
Ability to follow scripts while maintaining a natural, friendly tone
Accurate and timely data entry
Confidentiality with donor and medical information
Flexibility for occasional long or unscheduled hours during urgent blood needs
 Best Fit
This role is ideal for:
Someone who lives in the Oklahoma City area and is comfortable making outbound calls all day
People who want mission-driven work with a nonprofit that has a direct community impact
Participants who are friendly, persistent, and comfortable with a hybrid schedule
Anyone motivated by retention bonuses and steady raises in a stable nonprofit environment
Not a Good Fit for:
Participants who do not live in or near Oklahoma City. This is a hybrid role requiring on-site presence
Anyone who cannot occasionally work extended or unscheduled hours during emergency blood needs
People who are uncomfortable with outbound calling and following scripts under productivity metrics
Anyone who needs predictable hours every single week without exception
 Top 10 Resume Keywords:
Outbound calling
Appointment scheduling
Donor relations
Customer service
Telemarketing
Call center metrics
Data entry
Script adherence
Nonprofit healthcare
Community outreach
notes:
Employee reviews consistently describe OBI as a supportive employer with good benefits, regular bonuses, and annual raises, though some reviews note long or unpredictable hours and a structured point system tied to performance metrics. Set expectations that this is a metrics-driven calling role, not a flexible schedule job, despite the listed hours.
The retention bonuses are worth highlighting directly to participants: $500 at six months and $1,000 at one year is real money for staying with the role.
Career Pathway: Donor Care Representative I → Donor Care Representative II → Senior Donor Care Representative → Donor Recruitment Coordinator → Donor Services Supervisor → Donor Services Manager
other:
Pay & Benefits
Pay: $15.00 to $20.00/hr based on education and experience. Plus a $500 bonus at 6 months and a $1,000 bonus at 1 year.
Shift: Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Note: the posting also states flexibility to work unscheduled or long hours during blood supply emergencies. This is not always a fixed 8-to-5.
Benefits: Health, dental, vision, life insurance, long-term disability, 401(k), paid time off, and annual tuition reimbursement.
 Equipment: OBI provides a computer for work purposes. Participant is responsible for home internet and a cell phone.
 Assessment Expected? Interviews at OBI are generally described as easy with basic behavioral questions like describing a time you went outside procedure to make something happen. The overall hiring process typically takes about one week and is rated favorably by candidates. Indeed
 Background Check: Not explicitly stated in posting but standard for nonprofit healthcare organizations handling donor records.
Drug Test: Not stated in posting.
training: Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
